instruction: `ds/ll.py::reverse` loses the last node when reversing a list. Reversing `[1, 2, 3]` yields `[2, 1]` instead of `[3, 2, 1]`, and reversing a single-element list yields an empty list. The traversal stops one node too early, so the final node is never linked into the reversed list.
gold_patch:
diff --git a/ds/ll.py b/ds/ll.py
--- a/ds/ll.py
+++ b/ds/ll.py
@@ -45,7 +45,7 @@
     """Reverse the list in place and return the new head."""
     prev = None
     cur = head
-    while cur.nxt is not None:
+    while cur is not None:
         nxt = cur.nxt
         cur.nxt = prev
         prev = cur
